Case study: Leamington (Leamington, Ontario, Canada)
Section: CASE STUDY OVERVIEW

**Case Name and Location:** CS58 is associated with a publication titled *"Planned retreat approaches to support resilience to climate change in Canada,"* hosted on the Natural Resources Canada (NRCan) Open Science and Technology Repository (DOI: 10.4095/328323). No specific community, region, or geographic sub-case is identifiable from the available source material.

**Hazard(s):** Not determinable from the reviewed source. The publication title references "climate change" broadly, but no specific hazard types are identified in the available content.

**Type of Retreat:** Not determinable from the reviewed source. The title references "planned retreat approaches" (plural), which may suggest a synthesis or review of multiple retreat approaches rather than a single program.

**Scale:** Not determinable from the reviewed source.

**Key Actors:** Not determinable from the reviewed source. The document is hosted on a NRCan federal government repository, indicating a connection to federal government research or policy activity, but the specific author(s), commissioning body, and funders cannot be confirmed without the full text.

**Timeline:** Not determinable from the reviewed source.

**Key Outcomes:** Not determinable from the reviewed source.

**Narrative Summary:**

The single source document available for Case ID CS58 is a Natural Resources Canada (NRCan) Open Science and Technology Repository landing page for a publication titled *"Planned retreat approaches to support resilience to climate change in Canada"* (DOI: 10.4095/328323). The automated capture of this page retrieved only repository navigation elements, bilingual headers, image references, and institutional branding — no substantive body text from the publication itself was captured. As a result, no case-specific factual information can be extracted from this source.

It is not possible, on the basis of the captured content alone, to determine what community or communities are described, what hazard or hazards are addressed, what type or scale of managed retreat is discussed, who the key actors are, or what outcomes were achieved or assessed. The publication title suggests the document may be a national-level review or synthesis of planned retreat approaches in Canada rather than a single community-level case study, but this cannot be confirmed. The use of "approaches" (plural) in the title is suggestive of comparative or multi-case coverage, but this remains speculative.

This memo functions as a placeholder pending full-text retrieval of the NRCan publication. All questionnaire fields are coded N/A. Researchers should obtain the full text of the report directly from the NRCan Open Science and Technology Repository or by contacting the publisher, in order to complete coding and narrative synthesis for this case study.

Case study: Leamington (Leamington, Ontario, Canada)
Section: ADDITIONAL NOTES AND LESSONS LEARNED

**1. Critical Source Limitation — Placeholder Status of This Memo**
The single source document associated with CS58 is an automated capture of a government repository landing page containing no body text. The capture retrieved only navigation elements, bilingual institutional headers, image references, and repository branding. No substantive content from the NRCan report was captured. This memo must be treated as a placeholder. No questionnaire category can be meaningfully coded until the full text of the report is obtained.

**2. Likely Nature of the Source — Possible Synthesis Document**
Based solely on the publication title, this NRCan publication appears likely to be a national-level review or synthesis of planned retreat approaches across Canada, rather than a single community-level case study. If this interpretation is correct upon full-text retrieval, the document may function in the systematic review database as a source for multiple sub-cases, or as a meta-level review that contextualizes other Canadian managed retreat cases, rather than as a standalone case study. The appropriate role of CS58 within the review framework should be clarified once the full text is obtained.

**3. Terminology Observation — Title-Level Only**
The publication uses the term "planned retreat" rather than "managed retreat," "buyout," "relocation," or "resettlement." This is a title-level terminological observation only. It does not constitute evidence of how language was used in community engagement or program implementation, and it is not sufficient to assign any codebook framing category. Any interpretive significance of this terminology choice should be assessed against the full text.

**4. Recommendations for Follow-Up**
Researchers should:
- Obtain the full PDF of the NRCan report directly from the Open Science and Technology Repository or by contacting NRCan (DOI: 10.4095/328323).
- Determine whether this document covers a single case or multiple sub-cases, and adjust the case coding strategy accordingly.
- Cross-reference with other Canadian managed retreat case studies documented elsewhere in the systematic review database to assess whether CS58 overlaps with or supplements other coded cases. Specific sub-cases mentioned in the full report should be identified upon full-text retrieval; no sub-case names are derivable from the landing page content alone.

*Note on Audit Disagreements:* No audit findings are disputed in this Version 2. All flagged issues have been resolved as recommended by the Check 1 audit report. In particular, the specific Canadian program names (DMAF, National Flood Insurance Program reform, disaster financial assistance arrangements) cited in Version 1's Additional Notes without source support have been removed entirely, as has the list of named Canadian sub-case examples (Île Bizard, Grand Forks BC, Nova Scotia communities), which were unsourced against the CS58 document.
